Q: Designing a Thread-Safe, High-Performance Logging System in Modern C++ (C++17/20) A:

Regarding performance, I do not recommend C++ streams stuff which tend to be often pretty slow. That being said if is quite featureful and stable. So the best choice depend of the amount feature practically needed and the maintenance overheads vs performance trade-off. The best performance-wise is SIMD-optimised code (either specialised libraries or low-level C/C+ code).

Another key point regarding performance is to reduce allocations as much as possible since allocators tend not to scale. Indeed, logging can slow down other thread due to contention if a lot of allocations are performed (common). Buffering, stack allocations, message/buffer recycling, thread-local allocators are the key to reduce such overhead.

Buffering also help to reduce lock contention between the thread (pretty expensive on many-core systems).

I agree that using a specific worker for this task seems a good idea (especially when it comes to flexibility/extensibility). Be aware that locality matter for performance in such a case (especially on NUMA systems -- e.g. most modern AMD CPUs). Also please note that it inherently increase latency (same for buffering). Besides, keep in mind that there is a trade-off between latency and throughput, so a very low-latency often means a clearly sub-optimal throughput (possibly a pretty low one for extreme cases). The opposite is also clearly true. You should choose which one to flavour and accept the consequence (if you choose both then you will certainly get none of the two).

By the way, one important point with logging is the ordering of the message. A logging system much generally ensure some basic consistency property for them to be reliable. If a thread A logging an event E1 communicate with another thread B so to trigger an event E2 then also logged, you certainly expect E1 to appear before E2 in the logs. Otherwise the (weak) causality of the logs is broken. This is not always guaranteed by default, especially with a logging worker thread. Moreover, ensuring a rather strong consistency tends to reduce performance (and results in stall) compared to designs based on weak consistency. Please note that naive approach like storing the time in the log (and possibly reordering them) is not reliable since the system time is not monotonic, and per-thread clock are generally not sync by default. Using a global clock with global locks works but it can be very slow on many-core systems. I strongly advise you to read about vector clock

Retrospectively, I think you should define what kind of system is targetted if you want to focus on high-performance. So far I considered server systems which usually have dozens of cores and can now reach hundreds of them for recent high-end one. That being said, if you focus on mid-end mainstream client (x86-64) CPUs, there is far less issues to consider, especially if your application does not flood too much the logging system.

Q: Why does recursion in scheme macro cause error A:

If I may take the liberty of assuming that you don't actually care about factorial and are more interested in learning about recursive macros, then or is a classic example.

(define-syntax or
  (syntax-rules ()
    [(_) #f]
    [(_ e) e]
    [(_ e1 e2 e3 ...)
     (let ([t e1]) (if t t (or e2 e3 ...)))]))

Incremental expansion example:

;; Original
(or (f x) (g y z) "error")

;; First expansion
(let ([t (f x)])
  (if t
      t
      (or (g y z) "error")))

;; Second expansion
(let ([t (f x)])
  (if t
      t
      (let ([t (g y z)])
        (if t
            t
            (or "error")))))

;; Third expansion
(let ([t (f x)])
  (if t
      t
      (let ([t (g y z)])
        (if t
            t
            "error"))))

The or macro makes for a more realistic example because the recursive process operates on the syntactic structure -- a list of arbitrary expressions -- whereas fact requires a single, highly specific argument -- a positive integer literal -- and doesn't have any real work to do besides unwrapping the argument and handing it off to the factorial procedure.

As a general rule, if you find yourself writing a macro that cares about the structure of a pattern variable other than checking if it's an identifier or a pair, then there's probably a better solution.

Q: How can I exclude archived livestreams but keep premieres that appear in /videos? A:

Is there an official YouTube Data API field for this, or is matching the Videos tab impossible with YoutubeData API?

Nope. The Youtube front-end is not based on the public Youtube API. The front-end chooses (somehow) to label uploads as belonging to "streams" or "video" or "shorts" etc. These labels are not in the public API. Another example is direct video file links. The front-end knows them for actual playback, but the API doesn't reveal them in any returned response.

Currently, the best solution for "I’m trying to match a channel’s public Videos tab" is to just check the page's source for that info. Go to the "Videos" tab (and maybe one of its sub-options like "latest", "popular", "members" etc) and just save that page manually through your browser.

You can also try by code:

import urllib.request as urlreq

#video_id = "IcZxVrRrzcM"
#video_id = "6-qDqVXDZbY"

print("Paste your video ID:")
video_id = input()

url = 'https://www.youtube.com/@LiquidZulu/videos'

req = urlreq.Request(url)
client = urlreq.urlopen(req)
txt_html = (client.read(1499999).decode('utf-8'))

try:
  result = txt_html.index(video_id)
  print( 'VideoID:', video_id , 'is from tab "videos"' )
except:
  print( 'VideoID:', video_id , 'was NOT FOUND in "videos"' )

PS: Regarding What you mean by "Another example is direct video file links"?

Testing a "streams" upload: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xrY855jOlXo ...
Example of a Youtube direct video file link. You can see it's just the video (picture) only, because the sound part is in a different file (usually as .m4a file). The Youtube API response does not reveal these direct links. (note: Youtube will automatically expire this direct link in a few hours).

Q: Is there a cross-platform way to terminate all child (and grandchild) processes when the main process ends abnormally? A:

It's simpler for the child processes to periodically query the status of the main process. It's also better than "killing"; since it allows for a graceful shutdown for the child processes. And there is no "extra" process that needs to handle this; which begs how that process would start after the main process fails.

Q: ArgumentError in Users#new First argument in form cannot contain nil or be empty A:

It means that your @user object was not initialized..

You need to initialize your @user variable. Here are a couple of options.

Make sure your new method initializes it in your UsersController class:

def new
  @user = User.new
end

Another option is to just use a new object right in the form:

<%= form_for(User.new) do |f| %>

And yet another option, is to in your view, before echoing the form_for, put:

<% @user = User.new %>

My best recommendation would be to put the variable in the controller like I did in the first example.

Q: RegEx for C++ class parser A:

You can try this. However you have an awful lot of capture buffers.
I'm sure that's because you're in debug mode.
In the future, reduce capture buffers to ones that don't overlap.

The theory goes that you'd want to parse the line positional like or columnar like.
From left to right describe items that are of the same kind. Put these items
in the same column.
Proceed to define all your columns of like items.

Put the column that defines the actual variable names last.
This is where most of the regex naming constructs like classes go.

Since some of these columns are optional, the engine will actually try to use what should
have been optionally matched as the variable name downstream if necessary.

To avoid that you have to make it force match an optional column thereby
making it fail the match on incompleteness or ambiguity.

Example:

Optional Column 1 list
(?: AA | BB | CC )?

Optional Column 2 list
(?: XX | YY | ZZ )?

Required Column 3 Types
(Forces a match on optional items to be made above. Cannot be used as a type name) \b (?! (?: Automobile | AA | BB | CC | XX | YY | ZZ ) \b) [a-zA-Z_] [a-zA-Z0-9_]* \s*

Note that at this point here any optional columns would have been forced matched by the Type
segment. Presumably, no more Column 1 & 2 assertions need to be made going forward.

Here only the naming exclusions need to be made ( like (?! Automobile ), etc .. )

The apparent fix for your regex appears to be this.
It's up to you to fully formulate it into it's usable form using these guides.

https://regex101.com/r/RXNXS4/1

^ 
(                             # (1 start)
   \s* 
   (                             # (2 start)
      (?:
         virtual
       | inline
       | constexpr
       | static
       | friend
       | override
      )
      \s+ 
      (?: explicit \s+ )?
   )?                            # (2 end)
   (                             # (3 start), Return type
                                    # Exclude non-types. Must be matched above or elsewhere
      (?!
         (?: Automobile | virtual | inline | constexpr | static | friend | override | explicit )
         \b 
      )
      [a-zA-Z_] [a-zA-Z0-9_]* \s* 
   )                             # (3 end)
   \b 
   (                             # (4 start)
      (                             # (5 start)
         Automobile::
         (?! Automobile )
         [a-zA-Z_] [a-zA-Z0-9_]* 
      )                             # (5 end)
    | (                             # (6 start)
         (?! Automobile )
         [a-zA-Z_] [a-zA-Z0-9_]* 
         (?! :: )
      )                             # (6 end)
   )                             # (4 end)
)                             # (1 end)
.+

Q: PDF Compression Techniques A:

PDFs are already compressed in a number of ways, which prevents the external compression utilities from gaining much ground. It should be obvious that if you unpack the PDF, then the external utilities would have an easier time finding redundancies and patterns to compress.

I know of no tool to unpack the PDF without reprinting it though. Ghostscript can reprint the exiting PDF into a new PDF, and we can tell it to avoid compression in that second version.

gs -dCompressPages=false -dCompressFonts=false -dCompressStreams=false -dEncodeColorImages=false -dEncodeGrayImages=false -dEncodeMonoImages=false -dNOPAUSE -dBATCH -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dPDFSETTINGS=/screen -dSubsetFonts=true -dColorImageResolution=96 -dGrayImageResolution=96 -sOutputFile=raw-copy.pdf src.pdf

Even though the resulting copy is large (as it uses no compression), it can be more effectively packed with external tools

zpaq a raw-copy.pdf.zpaq raw-copy.pdf -m56,25,3 -fragment 9
zstd --ultra -22 raw-copy.pdf

A useful side effect is that we can compress together different versions of a text (unpacked PDFs, unpacked EPUBs, HTMLs, DOCs, RTFs and so on), eliminating redundancy and saving storage space across formats.

p.s. Sometimes the modified https://github.com/kaitz/zpaqf is better than the original in compressing PDFs, it depends on the PDF.
